title: Evaluation of Elective Surgery Patient Profiles and Service Quality in the Operating Room: A Study at Adam Malik Hospital, Medan
abstract: Background: Elective surgery is a planned medical procedure requires optimal coordination from the pre-operativeto post-operativephases. As a national referral hospital, Adam Malik Hospital in Medan handles a high volume of elective procedures, making the evaluation of service quality essential. Objective: This study aimed to describe patient characteristics and assess service quality in the operating room of ahospital. Methods: A descriptive quantitative study with a cross-sectional approach was conducted, involving 580 patients undergoing elective surgery. Service quality was assessed using objective clinical indicators, including the punctuality of the anesthesiologist and surgeon, the time from patient entry into the operating room to anesthesia induction, the interval between anesthesia induction and surgical incision, and the postoperative pain score. Data were collected from medical records and analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS). Results: Most patients were aged 18–40 years (48.8%), with a mean age of 40.5 ± 22.42 years. Females accounted for 53.8% of the samples, and the majority were classified as ASA III (44.7%). title: Effectiveness of Health Cadres Counseling in Preventing Child Sexual Abuse Among Mothers: A Quasi-Experimental Study in Bogor
abstract: Background: Child sexual abuse (CSA) in the world are seriously problems which affect the cause of death of children addition to disease. Research on appropriate approaches to Sexual Abuse Prevention in Toddlers Remains Limited in Indonesia, especially of the ones conducted on the outskirts of the capital city Jakarta. KemenPPPA (2023) reporting more than 15,000 cases (40 cases per day). Objective: To determine the effectiveness of counseling intervention by health cadres in preventing child sexual abuse among mother. Methods: A year-long study aims at pioneering a development of the health communication pre-post intervention models in preventing the occurrence of CSA in Bogor. The models comprise of individual and group counseling, given by the Integrated Health Services Cadres (Kader Posyandu), to educate the mothers about child sexual abuse prevention. Additionally, the study used randomized sample of 240 mothers-with-toddlers who were equally distributed to the individual-counseling groups, the focused-group-counseling groups, or controlled groups, and 15 health service staff from three districts in Bogor namely East Bogor, Central Bogor, and West Bogor. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: A Brief and Focused Training Model: Improving Health Volunteers’ Capacity to Promote Cervical Cancer Screening
abstract: Background: Community health volunteers (CHVs)- a subset of the broader community health workers, has led various health promotion initiatives of cervical cancer screening in Indonesia and across many LMICs. Capacity-building strengthens the roles of health volunteers, but little is documented about effective training designs considering resource-constraints and multiple roles of volunteers. Intensive, brief-duration training has emerged as an effective strategy for addressing such challenges. Objective: The effectiveness of a brief and focused training on CHVs' cervical cancer screening promotion knowledge, beliefs, and self-efficacy was assessed in this study. Methods: A six-hour training intervention was implemented using quasi-experimental, pre–post design with 103 health volunteers in Malang, Indonesia. Pre-test and post-test surveys were used to evaluate changes in knowledge, belief systems, and self-efficacy. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS, and data visualizations were performed using R Studio. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Adoption of Telehealth Services for Metabolic Syndrome: The Moderating Role of Health Consciousness in The UTAUT2 Model
abstract: Background: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) has become a major public health concern worldwide and is highly prevalent among office workers owing to their sedentary lifestyles and unhealthy behavioral patterns. Limited access to conventional healthcare services hinders preventive care and disease management in these regions. Telehealth has emerged as a promising solution, providing accessible, flexible, and cost-effective healthcare services. However, evidence regarding the factors influencing telehealth adoption among office workers at risk of MetS in developing countries is limited. Objective: This study aimed to examine the determinants of intention to use and actual use of telehealth services among Indonesian office workers at risk of MetS by extending the UTAUT2 model through the incorporation of health consciousness. Methods: A cross-sectional quantitative study was conducted involving 385 office workers identified as being at risk of developing MetS. Data were collected using an online questionnaire and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Menstrual Duration Among Reproductive Age Women Using E-Cigarettes in Malang: A Descriptive Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background:The diversification of cigarette products, including electronic cigarettes (e-cigarettes), has led to increased acceptance of female smoking, especially in urban areas. The absence of regulation by the Indonesian Food and Drug Authority (BPOM) regarding nicotine content in e-cigarettes raises concerns over uncontrolled nicotine exposure. Such exposure may impact the female reproductive system and disrupt hormonal balance, which is closely associated with menstrual cycle length and regularity. Purpose: This study aims to describe the duration of menstruation in e-cigarette users among women of childbearing age. Method: This type of research is a quantitative descriptive design with a cross-sectional approach. A total of 49 respondents, selected through purposive sampling from an e-cigarette user community in Malang City, participated based on inclusion criteria. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Data were analyzed using univariate analysis and descriptive statistics using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 26. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Smoking Behavior Factors Among Final-Year Engineering Students at UPN Veteran Jakarta
abstract: Background: The World Health Organization (WHO) reported that in 2022, approximately 1.25 billion people aged 15 and over worldwide were smokers. ASEAN countries contribute 10% of the world's total smokers, with Indonesia having the highest smoking prevalence, exceeding 50%. The Central Statistics Agency of DKI Jakarta Province (2024) reported that 22.56% of the population aged 15 years and older are smokers, with 13.39% of smokers in South Jakarta aged 18-24. Several factors influence smoking behavior, including the ease of obtaining cigarettes, peer conformity, family roles, and academic stress. These factors have been widely studied as significant determinants of smoking behavior, particularly among final-year university students who face educational and social pressures. Objective: This study aims to examine the factors influencing smoking behavior among final-year Mechanical Engineering students at UPN Veteran Jakarta. Methods: This study use a quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design. A total of 70 respondents were selected through total sampling from the final-year students of the Mechanical Engineering Study Program at UPN Veteran Jakarta. Data were collected bet

journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Do Journalists Make Better Researchers: Case Study Of Journalists As Primary Instrument In Qualitative Data Collection
abstract: Background: The National Health and Morbidity Survey 2022 found that the current prevalence of tobacco product use among Malaysian adolescents is 18.5%, with the majority (14.9%) using electronic cigarettes and vapes (ECVs) (Institute for Public Health, Ministry of Health, 2022). The increased prevalence of young girls using ECVs is particularly concerning, since smoking is not commonly the norm among girls and women. Objective: This case study aimed to unpack the disadvantages and advantages of a journalist reporting on the research topic, to also take on the role of a researcher, and the ethical considerations involved. Methods: This research comprised in-depth interviews with ECV users and stakeholders representing academia, the Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH), and the industry. Results: The results indicate that ECV use is viewed by both men and women mainly as a health issue, as there is no difference in how males and females respond to 14 of the Health Belief Model (HBM) perceptions. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Adolescents’ Perceptions Toward Pictorial Health Warnings on Cigarette Packs in South Kalimantan
abstract: Background: Smoking is a unique social phenomenon among adolescents because it begins with high curiosity to try cigarettes and eventually develops into a habit that is difficult to stop. Objectives: This research aims to explore adolescents' perceptions of pictorial health warnings (PHWs) on cigarette packs. Method: This research is qualitative, using a purposive sampling technique with predetermined criteria. The population was male adolescents aged 10-19 years. This research involved 35 adolescents from Banjarmasin City, Banjarbaru City, and Tanah Bumbu Regency, South Kalimantan Province. Data were collected using an open-ended questionnaire. Results: The findings of this research can be grouped into several main thematic areas, namely perceptions of visual content, effectiveness of pictorial health warnings (PHWs), suggestions for improvement, emotional responses, and intensity of attention. Participants generally thought that the images displayed on cigarette packs should more explicitly highlight the health effects of smoking. title: Innovative Approaches to Mental Health: A Systematic Review of Culturally-Based Counseling In Diverse Societies
abstract: Background: Mental health is a fundamental component of human well-being, yet the growing prevalence of psychological disorders across culturally diverse populations has challenged the effectiveness of conventional counseling approaches. Culturally-based counseling has emerged as an innovative approach that integrates cultural values, beliefs, languages, and identities into therapeutic processes to improve engagement and treatment outcomes. Despite increasing interest in this approach, a comprehensive global synthesis of its effectiveness and implementation remains limited. Objective: This review aims to identify and arrange strategies that can be implemented to enhance adolescent STIs prevention and screening behaviors. Methods: This systematic literature review (SLR), registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251127039), synthesized evidence from 16 primary studies published between 2020 and 2025. Articles were retrieved from six major databases and Google Scholar following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Digital Snakes and Ladders Game Promoting Fruit and Vegetable Consumption in Adolescents
abstract: Background: Fruit and vegetable consumption behaviour among adolescents is very low, especially among adolescents aged 10-14 years. Teenagers tend to consume fast food such as sausages, hamburgers, and meatballs. One of the factors that influences this is the low level of knowledge about fruit and vegetable consumption. To improve adolescents' knowledge and behaviour in accordance with their characteristics, digital application-based games are used. Objective: To develop an educational model that improves vegetable and fruit consumption knowledge, attitude, and behaviour among adolescents. Methods: This research uses a mixed-method study design with the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation (ADDIE) approach to create and test applications. The field test was conducted at SMPN 2 Muaro Jambi with 40 respondents selected using proportional random sampling who met the criteria. Comprehensive data collection through observation, interviews, questionnaires, Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ) instruments, and Focus Group Discussion, one-on-one testing, small group testing, and experimentation in field trials. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Development of an HBM-Based Health Coaching Module to Enhance Adolescents’ Self-Efficacy: Research and Development Study for Preventing Reproductive and Behavioral Health Risks
abstract: Background: Adolescence is a critical period in individual development, marked by increased vulnerability to various risk behaviors, including those categorized under the Triad of Adolescent Reproductive Health (sexuality, HIV/AIDS, drug abuse). Low self-efficacy is one of the key factors influencing adolescents’ tendency to engage in or poorly cope with these risks. Objective: This study aims to develop a health coaching intervention module based on the Health Belief Model as an effort to enhance adolescents’ self-efficacy in preventing risks associated with the Adolescent Reproductive Health Triad (sexuality, HIV/AIDS, and drug abuse). Methods: The research method employed is Research and Development (R&D), using a modified Borg and Gall model approach. The study involved 100 adolescents aged 15–18 years, selected through a quota sampling technique. Before its use in data collection, the module underwent expert validation and a pilot testing phase. Results: The results of the module development indicate that the module is feasible in terms of content, presentation, and practicality. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Social Support from Correctional Counselors for Inmates: A Phenomenological Study at Class IIA Correctional Facility in Jember
abstract: Background: Inmates are a vulnerable group prone to mental health disorders due to internal pressures such as loss of freedom, guilt, and depression, as well as external pressures such as social stigma and weakened family relationships. Preliminary data at the Class IIA Correctional Facility in Jember indicated that inmates frequently experience severe stress, anxiety, and a significant decrease in daily motivation. In this context, social support plays a vital role in maintaining their mental stability, particularly the support provided by correctional counselors (wali pemasyarakatan), who maintain close and regular interactions with them. Objective: To explore the specific forms of social support provided by correctional counselors to inmates at Class IIA Correctional Facility in Jember based on House’s social support framework. Methods: This study employed a qualitative approach using a phenomenological method. Informants consisted of one key informant (Head of the Health and Care Guidance Subsection), four main informants (correctional counselors), and three additional informants (inmates), selected through purposive sampling. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Knowledge, Attitude, and Myth Beliefs Related to Menstrual Hygiene Among Female Students
abstract: Background: Menstrual hygiene remains a concern in Islamic boarding schools owing to limited access to information and the strong influence of inherited myths. A preliminary survey at the Darul Huffaz Islamic Boarding School revealed that some female students were reluctant to wash their hair during menstruation and lacked awareness of genital hygiene due to myth-based beliefs. A previous study in Bandar Lampung found that 60% of adolescent girls experienced itching during menstruation, and none had received specific education on menstrual hygiene. Objectives: This study aimed to examine female students’ knowledge, attitudes, and beliefs regarding menstrual hygiene behavior. Methods: This study employed a quantitative method with a cross-sectional design. A total of 211 female students were selected using a total sampling technique. Data were collected using Likert-scale and multiple-choice questionnaires and analyzed using the chi-square test. Results: 128 female students (75.3%) had good knowledge and hygiene practices, 119 (76.3%) had positive attitudes and good hygiene actions, and 136 (70.5%) were skeptical of myths and maintained good hygiene behavior. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Snake and Ladder-Based Stimulation Model: Enhancing Development in Children Aged 34–38 Months
abstract: Background: Early childhood development is a key indicator of future human resource quality. In Indonesia, the prevalence of developmental delays among toddlers, including those aged 34-38 months, remains high, highlighting the need for effective and easily implemented stimulation interventions. Objective: To develop a Snakes and Ladders stimulation model to improve the development of children aged 34-38 months. Methods: A pre-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design was employed with 21 children aged 34-38 months selected purposively in the working area of Mamboro Public Health Center during May–July 2025. Research instruments included the Developmental Pre-Screening Questionnaire (KPSP) and a media validation checklist. Data were analyzed using the Wilcoxon Signed Rank test. Results: Expert validation by three specialists yielded a score of 78.2% (valid category) with minor revisions. Statistical analysis revealed a significant improvement in child development post-intervention (p =0.000), with most children shifting from “questionable” to “appropriate” developmental categories. title: Subjective Experiences of Adolescents in Facing Obesity: A Phenomenological Approach
abstract: Background: Adolescent obesity has emerged as a global public health issue. Despite increasing prevalence, limited research explores adolescents’ subjective experiences and perceptions of obesity within their sociocultural context. Understanding these perspectives is crucial for developing comprehensive interventions that address not only the clinical but also the psychosocial dimensions of obesity. Objective: This study expected to provide a comprehensive and contextual understanding of the challenges, perceptions, and meanings that adolescents associate with obesity conditions, which can serve as the basis for the development of more sensitive and effective health interventions and psychosocial support Method: This qualitative study employed a phenomenological approach to explore the lived experiences of obese adolescents in Leuwisari District, Tasikmalaya, West Java. Fifteen adolescents were selected purposively based on the inclusion criteria. Data were collected through in-depth interviews using a semi-structured guide, then transcribed, coded, and analyzed thematically through textural and structural descriptions. title: Determinants of Postpartum Mothers’ Adherence to Iron–Folic Acid Tablet in Astambul Public Health Center, Banjar Regency, Indonesia
abstract: Background: Postpartum anemia remains a major global public health concern, particularly in low and middle income countries. Objective: This study aimed to examine the relationship and influence of knowledge, attitude, and social support on postpartum mothers’ adherence to iron–folic acid (IFA) supplementation. Methods: A cross-sectional design was applied with 40 respondents. The study was conducted among postpartum mothers receiving services at Astambul Public Health Center, Banjar Regency, Indonesia. Data were collected using questionnaires measuring knowledge, attitude, social support, and adherence. Spearman’s rho correlation test was used to assess relationships between variables, while binary logistic regression was employed to identify the main predictors of adherence. title: Evaluating Quality Governance on Patient Safety: Qualitative Study at Lampung Health Centers
abstract: Background: Patient safety is a system aimed at improving safety in healthcare services to prevent harm from medical errors. In 2019, Indonesia recorded 7,465 patient safety incidents, indicating persistent challenges in improving healthcare quality. East Lampung Regency, with 34 Community Health Centers, reflects similar issues, making it a relevant setting for examining the quality of governance in primary care. Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of quality governance on Patient Safety Incident (PSI) performance at Community Health Centers in East Lampung from 2023 to 2024. Methods: A qualitative approach was applied using in-depth interviews, observations, and document reviews at three centers representing different accreditation levels (Paripurna, Main, and Madya). A total of 11 informants were purposively selected, including health center leaders, quality officers, health office officials, and service users. Data triangulation was conducted across multiple sources to ensure consistency and reliability, supported by cross-validation between interviews, observations, and documents. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Interventions for Adolescent STIs: A Scoping Review of Prevention and Screening Strategies
abstract: Background: The prevalence of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) in adolescents is on the rise annually. Various initiatives have been implemented to mitigate morbidity and mortality rates. However, the incidence of STIs among adolescents remains alarmingly high, highlighting the need to strengthen preventive measures and expand access to high-quality screening services. Objective: To identify and categorize strategies for improving prevention and screening behaviors relate to STIs among adolescents. Method: The investigation employed a comprehensive review design. Articles were procured from four databases: PubMed, ProQuest, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science. All articles were evaluated for their suitability to address the research questions using the Population, Concept, Context (PCC) as well as inclusion and exclusion criteria. Article screening was conducted using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses for Scoping Review (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines (2020), and the Guidance for Conducting Systematic Scoping Review (2015) was followed to extract the data. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: From Campus to Lifestyle: What Really Drives Anemia-Preventive Behaviors in Female Islamic College Students?
abstract: Background: Iron deficiency anemia is a significant public health concern among women of reproductive age, including female college students. Anemia can impair immunity, physical fitness, and concentration, and increase the risk of future pregnancy complications. Although prevention efforts such as the provision of iron–folic acid (IFA) tablets have been implemented, female college students have not been a primary target of interventions and remain vulnerable due to unbalanced dietary patterns and unhealthy eating habits. Data from the Faculty of Health Sciences, UIN Syarif Hidayatullah Jakarta, reported an anemia prevalence of 46.07% among female college students. Anemia prevention behavior is shaped by predisposing, enabling, and reinforcing factors; however, research on determinants of such behavior in this population remains limited. Objective: This study aimed to identify factors associated with anemia prevention behavior among female students at the Faculty of Health Sciences in 2025. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Developing Cadres' Personal Skills in TB Prevention through Communication Training and E-TIBI
abstract: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a global public health challenge and is a key priority under Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3. In 2024, 17 suspected cases and 4 confirmed cases of TB were identified in Menang Village, Kediri Regency. Health cadres play an important role in TB control and need adequate communication skills and digital competence. In line with the Ottawa Charter for Health Promotion, particularly Develop Personal Skills, strengthening cadres’ knowledge and skills is important to support TB prevention and early detection in the community. Therefore, effective communication training and initial socialization of the E-TIBI application were implemented to develop cadres’ personal skills. Objective: This study aimed to analyze the outcomes of effective communication training and initial socialization of the E-TIBI application in developing the personal skills of health cadres. Methods: This study utilized a quasi-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design involving 23 health cadres in Menang Village, Kediri Regency. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Social Determinants of Health of Psychological Injury Incidents In Early Adolescents
abstract: Background: Psychological injury among early adolescents has become a significant public health concern globally and in Indonesia. This study examines how social determinants of health influence psychological injury among early adolescents in Makassar City. Objective: To analyze the relationship between social determinants of health and psychological injury among early adolescents in Makassar City using a comprehensive multivariate approach. Methods: This quantitative research employed a cross-sectional design involving 384 early adolescents aged 10-14 years. Participants were selected through multi-stage random sampling from 12 schools across Makassar City, ensuring representation of diverse socioeconomic profiles. Data were collected using validated instruments, including the Psychological Injury Scale for Adolescents (PISA), Family Environment Scale (FES), and Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support. Multivariate analysis using binary logistic regression was conducted to identify significant predictors while controlling for confounding variables. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Adolescent Girls Behavior Towards Reproductive Health Services regarding Personal Hygiene during Disaster: Systematic Review
abstract: Background: Natural disasters can trigger health crises and lead to the neglect of adolescents’ reproductive health. The risk of reproductive health problems among adolescents increases due to damaged sanitation facilities, such as urinary tract infections in Turkey (22.6%) and Jordan (92.25%). A total of 68% of households reported that their sanitation facilities were damaged, while 36% had no sanitation facilities three months after the disaster. In addition, 14% of adolescents were unaware that such services were available, and 12% felt ineligible to access them. Objective: This study was conducted to identify the factors that may influence adolescent girls’ access to reproductive health services related to personal hygiene during natural disasters. Methods: This study employed a systematic review approach using the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines. Through searches conducted in Scopus, ScienceDirect, and PubMed, 11 articles met the inclusion criteria. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Association Between Cigarette Advertising Exposure and Smoking Behavior Among Early Adolescents
abstract: Background: The prevalence of smoking among adolescents in Indonesia continues to increase, extending even to students at the elementary and junior high school levels. Adolescence is a crucial phase that is also vulnerable to the formation of long-term smoking behavior. One of the factors implicated in this trend is exposure to cigarette advertising disseminated through various channels, including social media platforms and outdoor promotional media. Objective: This study aimed to examine the association between exposure to cigarette advertisements and smoking behavior among elementary and junior high school students in Sleman Regency, Yogyakarta. Methods: A quantitative study with an observational analytical design and a cross-sectional approach was conducted. A total of 182 students were recruited using a cluster sampling technique. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire adapted from previously validated instruments. Univariate and bivariate analyses were performed, with the chi-square test applied to assess the relationship between advertisement exposure and smoking behavior. Results: Most respondents reported a moderate level of exposure to cigarette advertising

journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Perceived Academic Stress, Emotional Eating, and Depressive Symptoms among FK-KMK UGM Students
abstract: Background: In Indonesia, 6.2% of people between the ages of 15 and 24 suffer from depression, which is especially common among college students enrolled in health-related courses. Previous research has demonstrated a favorable correlation between depressive symptoms and perceived academic stress. Emotional eating, or eating to cope with unpleasant feelings, is one unhealthy coping mechanism. Objective: In this study, undergraduate students at Universitas Gadjah Mada’s Faculty of Medicine, Public Health, and Nursing (FK-KMK UGM) were asked whether emotional eating moderates the association between perceived academic stress and depressive symptoms. Methods: 416 undergraduate students from the academic years 2021–2024 participated in this cross-sectional survey. The Beck Depression Inventory II (BDI-II), the Perception of Academic Stress (PAS) questionnaire, and the Emotional Eating Scale (EES) were used to evaluate depressive symptoms. Convenience sampling was employed, and Google Forms was utilized to gather data via WhatsApp and LINE groups. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Preconception Nutrition Intervention Models for Adolescent Girls: Intergenerational Stunting Scoping Review
abstract: Background: Stunting is still a significant global public health problem. In Indonesia, the prevalence of stunting decreased from 24.4% in 2021 to 21.6% in 2022, but the figure is still above the expected target. Nutritional interventions in the preconception period, especially in adolescent girls as mothers-to-be, are seen as an important strategy to prevent intergenerational stunting. However, evidence on the most effective intervention models is still scattered and has not been comprehensively synthesized. Objective: To map the scientific evidence on the model of preconception nutritional intervention in adolescent girls and its contribution to the prevention of intergenerational stunting during the period 2020–2026. Methods: This study used a systematic scoping review method based on the Arksey and O'Malley framework updated by Levac et al. (2010) and followed the PRISMA-ScR 2018 guidelines. Literature searches were conducted on PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar. Inclusion criteria included studies in adolescent girls aged 10–19 years who implemented preconception nutrition interventions with outcomes related to nutritional status or s

journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Disaster Preparedness in Disaster-Prone Areas: A Scoping Review and Implications for Health Resilience
abstract: Background: Over the past decade, natural hazard events have become increasingly frequent and severe worldwide, highlighting the importance of community preparedness to protect health and well-being during emergencies. Although disaster risk reduction has been extensively studied, empirical evidence remains limited on the actual preparedness of residents and households, particularly regarding the extent to which disaster knowledge is translated into practical preparedness actions. Objective: This scoping review aimed to map the current state of disaster preparedness among residents and households in disaster-prone areas worldwide. Methods: Relevant studies were searched for across PubMed, ScienceDirect, Wiley Online Library, and Scopus, following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and using relevant keywords, including “disaster preparedness” and “disaster-prone area”. The search covered the period from January 1, 2020, to February 28, 2025. Articles were screened against predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, and a quality appraisal was conducted to assess the methodological quality of the included studies. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: The Phenomenology of Healthcare Service: Young Women’s Experiences of Accessing National Health Insurance
abstract: Background: The National Health Insurance (Indonesia's universal healthcare program), as a social protection mechanism, faces challenges related to the regularity and quality of service provision, especially for vulnerable groups such as young women. Objective: This study aims to explore the subjective experiences of young women aged 17 to 25 years in using BPJS services in hospitals, emphasizing the interactive, emotional, and social factors that shape their perspectives. Methods: This research used a qualitative phenomenological methodology. Data were collected through snowball sampling techniques, followed by in-depth interviews with 18 young female participants aged 17 to 25 years old. The data were then processed using Miles and Huberman's analysis technique, which involved data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The writer also used triangulation techniques to validate the processed data. Results: Experiences of young women utilizing BPJS are marked by a duality between financial security and uncertainty about service supply. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Mental Health Literacy Interventions for Preventing Bullying among High School Students
abstract: Background: Health, which refers to a complete physical, mental, and social well-being, enables individuals to live productively in their social and economic contexts. Recently, Indonesian society has been alarmed by the increasing number of cases related to children's health, both physically, such as the rising number of children experiencing obesity and stunting, and psychologically. Another urgent issue requiring special attention is the prevalence of school-aged children experiencing depression due to bullying. The incidence of bullying among students continues to rise across various educational levels, necessitating preventive measures and effective interventions. Objective: To analyze the level of students’ knowledge regarding bullying and to evaluate the effectiveness of a mental health literacy intervention. Methods: Employing a one-group pre-test–post-test quantitative descriptive design, this study involved 49 respondents selected through purposive sampling from a total population of 132 students at SMA Muhammadiyah 6 Surakarta, consisting of 19 regular students and 30 inclusive students with various conditions (slow learners, autism, dwarfism, physical disabilities, low

title: Effectiveness of Community-Based Maternal Education and Screening in Improving Maternal Knowledge
abstract: Background: Maternal health remains a major public health priority. Maternal health literacy is essential for recognizing pregnancy danger signs and making timely use of maternal health services. Community-based education can improve knowledge, while integrating basic screening may increase the relevance of health messages by linking education with individual health assessment. Objective: This study evaluated changes in maternal health knowledge after an integrated community-based maternal health education and screening program among pregnant women in Bali, Indonesia. Methods: A quasi-experimental one-group pretest-posttest study was conducted among 15 pregnant women in Carangsari Village, Bali, recruited purposively from local maternal health services. The program combined education on pregnancy danger signs, maternal nutrition, anemia prevention, and oral health with hemoglobin testing, mid-upper arm circumference measurement, and oral health examination. Maternal knowledge was measured using the same structured questionnaire before and after the program. title: Postpartum Mothers’ Experiences of Consuming Traditional Herbal Medicine: Phenomenological Study to Increase Breast Milk Production among the Madurese, Indonesia
abstract: Background: The postpartum period is a challenging time for mothers. One common challenge during this period is low breast milk production, which can be caused by various internal and external factors. East Java Province reported that the lowest percentage of breast milk for children aged 0-23 months (toddlers) came from Sumenep Regency, namely 76.9%. Objective: To explore the experiences of postpartum mothers in consuming traditional herbal medicine to increase breast milk production. Method: This study used a qualitative design with a phenomenological approach. Eight informants were involved, including postpartum mothers, traditional herbal medicine sellers, midwives, and community leaders. Thematic analysis was used for data analysis. Results: The results of the study indicate that traditional herbal medicine is commonly consumed by postpartum mothers. It is typically consumed 1–2 days after childbirth to stimulate breast milk production. The traditional herbal medicine is composed of natural ingredients, including Javanese turmeric (temulawak), turmeric, and ginger, and is consumed twice daily. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Waek AI-Based Mental Health Promotion to Prevent Bullying Among Generation Z
abstract: Background: Generation Z, born between 1995 and 2010, has grown up in an era of rapid technological development in which digital media plays an important role in daily life. Although digital connectivity offers educational and social benefits, it also increases adolescents’ vulnerability to mental health problems and bullying, particularly in online environments. Bullying can negatively affect psychological well-being, self-esteem, academic achievement, and social relationships. Therefore, innovative mental health promotion strategies that are technology-based and attractive to adolescents are needed to improve bullying prevention awareness among Generation Z. Objective: This study aimed to examine the effectiveness of a Waek AI–based game application as a mental health nursing intervention for improving bullying prevention awareness among Generation Z. Methods: A quantitative quasi-experimental design with intervention and control groups was used in this study. A total of 90 participants were recruited and divided equally into intervention and control groups. title: Husband's Social Support in Preventing Peripartum Depression Among Third-Trimester Pregnant Women
abstract: Background: Peripartum depression may begin during pregnancy and continue after childbirth. Women in the third trimester commonly experience physical discomfort, hormonal changes, fear of childbirth, and concerns about maternal and infant safety, increasing their vulnerability to psychological distress. Husbands are the closest source of social support, yet their involvement is often limited to practical assistance rather than psychological support. Objective: This study explored husbands’ social support for third-trimester pregnant women in preventing peripartum depression and developed a pocketbook based on identified needs. Methods: A qualitative case-study design was conducted in the working area of Alai Public Health Center, Padang, from January to June 2026. Eleven informants were purposively selected, including three pregnant women, three husbands, three program officers, one media-design expert, and one language expert. Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews, field notes, and documentation and analyzed using data reduction, data display, conclusion drawing, and verification. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Prevention of Adolescent Smoking Through Community Asset Mapping and School-Based Risk Communication
abstract: Background: Adolescent smoking remains a major public health concern because it increases the risk of nicotine dependence and non-communicable diseases later in life. School-based smoking prevention programs have primarily focused on health education, while the integration of community assets and risk communication to support sustainable behavioral change remains limited. Objective: This study aimed to describe the implementation of Community Asset Mapping (CAM) and school-based risk communication as health promotion strategies for preventing smoking behavior among adolescents. Methods: A descriptive study with a participatory health promotion approach was conducted among 36 eleventh-grade students at SMKN 10 Samarinda, Indonesia. The intervention included identifying smoking-related risk factors, mapping community assets, developing risk communication strategies, designing health promotion media, and assessing health literacy and student empowerment using structured questionnaires. Data were analyzed descriptively using frequencies and percentages. Results: Most participants demonstrated good health literacy (83.3%) and good levels of student empowerment (66.7%). title: The Influence of Digital Health Literacy on Non-Healthcare Students' Telemedicine Interest
abstract: Background: The advancement of digital technology has improved the public’s ability to access health information and has encouraged students to use telemedicine services. Telemedicine has expanded access to healthcare services and health information. However, digital health literacy is considered essential for engaging with digital health services. Objectives: This study aimed to analyze the influence of digital competencies and health information literacy on non-health students’ interest in accessing telemedicine services at Muhammadiyah University of Yogyakarta. Methods: This research used a cross-sectional design and involved 104 students from non-health fields, selected through convenience sampling. Data were gathered using a Digital Health Literacy Competencies (DHLC) questionnaire and an adopted telemedicine interest questionnaire, both of which had been validated. Data analysis was carried out using univariate analysis and multiple linear regression with SPSS software. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: Effectiveness of a Family-Based HIV Intervention in Preventing Sexual Risk Behaviors Among Adolecents in Indonesia: A Quasi-Experimental Study
abstract: Background: Adolescents are a priority population for HIV prevention because knowledge, decision-making capacity, and perceptions of risk are still evolving during this developmental stage. Family engagement may enhance protective behaviors by strengthening communication, supervision, emotional support, and adolescents’ confidence in avoiding high-risk situations. Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a family-based HIV prevention intervention in improving sexual risk prevention behavior among adolescents in Bandung Regency, Indonesia. Methods: A quasi-experimental study with a pretest-posttest control-group design was conducted among 350 adolescents aged 16–18 years. Participants were assigned to an intervention group (n = 175) or a control group (n = 175). The intervention consisted of three weekly family-based educational sessions involving adolescents and caregivers, while the control group received standard HIV prevention information through leaflets. Outcomes were assessed using the Sexual Behavior Abstinence and Avoidance of High-Risk Situation Questionnaire, which measures self-efficacy, behavioral intention, and perceived benefit. journal_name: Jurnal Promkes: The Indonesian Journal of Health Promotion and Health Education
title: The Effect of Booklet-Based Nutrition Education on Mothers' Knowledge and Attitudes: A Quasi Experimental for Stunting Prevention
abstract: Background: Stunting remained a major public health challenge in Indonesia and adversely affected children's physical growth, cognitive development, and future productivity. Improving maternal knowledge and attitudes through nutrition education played an important role in preventing stunting during the first 1,000 days of life. Educational booklets provided structured, accessible, and easy-to-understand information, making them a useful medium for delivering health education. Objective: This study examined the effect of booklet-based nutrition education delivered through lectures on the knowledge and attitudes of mothers of children under five years of age regarding stunting prevention. Methods: This study used a quasi-experimental design with a one-group pretest-posttest approach. A total of 42 mothers of children under five years of age were selected using purposive sampling. Participants completed a 10-item knowledge questionnaire and a 10-item Likert-scale attitude questionnaire before and after the intervention. title: Adolescents’ Perspectives on Sugar-Sweetened Beverage Consumption: A Qualitative Study to Inform Health Promotion Strategies
abstract: Background: Sugar-sweetened beverage (SSB) consumption among adolescents is a public health concern because of its association with weight gain and obesity. Understanding adolescents’ experiences and perceptions is important for developing contextually relevant health promotion strategies. Objective: This study explored the experiences and perceptions of Gen-Z adolescents in Karawang regarding daily SSB consumption, focusing on attitudes, subjective norms, perceived behavioural control, and behavioural intentions based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). Methods: A descriptive qualitative study using a constructivist-interpretivist paradigm was conducted. Three Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), each involving eight adolescents aged 13–17 years, were conducted, resulting in 24 participants. Semi-structured interviews with teachers were also conducted for source triangulation. Data were analyzed thematically using both deductive and inductive approaches, guided by TPB constructs and emerging themes. title: The Effects of Personal and Environmental on The Incidence of Scabies
abstract: Background: Several common health issues frequently occur in Islamic boarding schools. Among the most common are scabies, shortness of breath, fever, fainting, coughs and colds accompanied by the flu, gastritis, and others. Scabies, also known as “gudik,” is a common skin disease among children, particularly in densely populated areas. Students living in Islamic boarding schools seem “bound” to experience this itchy condition, characterized by intense itching, skin rashes, and scratches. Personal hygiene, knowledge, and support from teachers and peers are among the contributing factors. Objective: This study aims to analyze the influence of personal factors (knowledge and self-efficacy) and environmental factors (social support, access to supplies, and observational learning) on the incidence of scabies, with personal hygiene practices serving as a mediating variable. Methods: This quantitative study used a cross-sectional design and was conducted at three Islamic boarding schools in the Lowokwaru subdistrict of Malang City.
